title: Conservatism

cards.b:
Conservatism is often dismissed as 'resisting change'. That is too simple. It is a way of thinking about society: be careful with inherited institutions, because they hold wisdom no single mind can design.

UPSC asks about it in Paper I as one of the main ideologies, and it links to Burke, Oakeshott and the New Right. Knowing its internal split makes your answer stand out.

Most conservative writers share a few instincts.

  • Tradition: customs carry accumulated experience.
  • Human imperfection: people are limited and flawed, so grand schemes fail.
  • Organic society: society grows like a living body, it is not a machine.
  • Hierarchy and authority: natural differences of role are normal.
  • Property: it gives security and a stake in order.

The founder-figure is Edmund Burke, in Reflections on the Revolution in France (1790). He attacked the revolution for tearing up the social contract between the dead, the living and the unborn.

His principle: a state without the means of some change is without the means of its conservation. So he accepted slow, careful reform. He did not oppose change as such.

Michael Oakeshott, Rationalism in Politics (1962), gave a modern version. The rationalist thinks politics is problem-solving by abstract reason and plans.

Oakeshott said real political knowledge is practical, learned by doing, like cooking skill and not a recipe book. Politics is 'sailing a boundless sea', where tradition is the only harbour. He preferred a state that keeps order and lets people pursue their own ends.
The One Nation tradition (Benjamin Disraeli) accepts social reform to avoid class war. The New Right mixes neoliberal economics with neoconservative social values: law and order, family, nation.

Conservatives take a darker view of people than liberals or socialists. Hobbes and Burke's followers see humans as insecure and prone to conflict. So order, authority and a strong state matter more than abstract rights.

This explains the stress on law and punishment, and doubt about egalitarian engineering. Compare Rousseau or Marx, who think society corrupts a basically good human being.

Critics raise four points.

  • It defends privilege by calling it tradition. Whose tradition? Women, slaves and the poor were excluded from 'inherited wisdom'.
  • It has no fixed content: it simply defends whatever exists, even bad institutions.
  • The New Right is self-contradictory: markets dissolve the very traditions it values.
  • Radical thinkers call it a mask for class power (Marx).

Be ready for comparison questions.

  • Liberalism: individual first. Conservatism: society and institutions first.
  • Socialism: equality by design. Conservatism: inequality is natural and useful.
  • Fascism: also anti-liberal, but it is revolutionary and mass-mobilising, while conservatism is cautious and elite-led.

Note the 'conservative liberal' overlap in economics, as with Hayek.

India has no party formally called conservative, but conservative ideas appear in many places. Gandhi's trust in village tradition, the Swatantra Party (1959) defending property and markets against Nehruvian planning, and cultural nationalism that cherishes civilisational heritage all show some of the themes.

The Constituent Assembly too showed Burkean caution: it kept British institutions and reformed them slowly. Also useful: Ambedkar warned that 'tradition' in caste society often protects hierarchy.

"Conservatism is not opposed to change but to a certain kind of change. Discuss."
"Distinguish paternalistic conservatism from the New Right."
"Examine Oakeshott's critique of rationalism in politics."

Structure: define conservatism, give the five themes, Burke and Oakeshott, the two strands, critique, then Indian example like the Swatantra Party.

quiz.q: Who wrote Reflections on the Revolution in France?

o: Neoliberal economics and neoconservative social values

quiz.q: For Burke society is a partnership between…
o: The dead, the living and the unborn

quiz.q: Conservatives generally view human nature as…
The Swatantra Party was formed in…
Which is a criticism of the New Right?
o: Markets erode the traditions it values
quiz.w: The market and tradition contradict each other.

quiz.q: Which differs from fascism in conservatism?
quiz.w: Conservatism is cautious, fascism is revolutionary.
